title: Prompt Engineering — The Free Lever
summary: Before touching architecture, the words in your system prompt and output-format constraints already determine a large fraction of your token spend.
whyItMatters: Output tokens are typically billed at a higher rate than input tokens, and a verbose or unconstrained system prompt is paid on every single call. This is the cheapest lever because it requires no new code paths, only better text.

concepts.heading: Output-length is a cost knob you control directly
concepts.body: Unconstrained, a model will often over-explain. Explicit output-format instructions (structured JSON, a word/line cap, 'no preamble') reduce output tokens directly, and output tokens are the more expensive side of the ledger on most model pricing.

concepts.heading: System prompt density vs. verbosity
concepts.body: Every token in the system prompt is paid on every call. Long, narrative system prompts read well to a human reviewer but cost the same each invocation. Dense, structured instructions (short imperative bullets, not prose) typically compress the same guidance into fewer tokens without losing precision.

concepts.heading: Few-shot examples are a cost/reliability tradeoff, not a free win
concepts.body: Each example in a few-shot prompt is paid on every call, forever. They meaningfully improve reliability for ambiguous or format-sensitive tasks, but for well-specified tasks a strong zero-shot instruction is often just as reliable and strictly cheaper. Default to zero-shot; add examples only when zero-shot demonstrably fails.

exercises.title: Quantify the cost of an unconstrained vs. constrained output format
exercises.goal: See directly how much an explicit output-format instruction saves in output tokens for the same task.
steps: Pick a real task your agent performs (e.g. 'summarize this support ticket and extract the customer's request').

Build a Strands agent and run the task once with a bare instruction and no format constraint. Record output tokens from response.metrics.accumulated_usage. → Expect: a free-form paragraph response, often 150-400 output tokens.

Run the identical task again, adding: 'Respond with only a JSON object: {"issue": string, "urgency": "low"|"medium"|"high"}. No other text.' → Expect: output tokens drop substantially, often by more than half, with equal or better usability for downstream code.
Compare the two accumulated_usage.get("outputTokens") values directly. → Expect: a concrete before/after number you can multiply by your call volume.

code.content:
from strands import Agent
from strands.models import BedrockModel

agent = Agent(model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5"))
ticket = "Customer says their order #4471 hasn't arrived after 2 weeks and they want a refund immediately."

# Unconstrained
resp_a = agent(f"Summarize this support ticket and extract the customer's request: {ticket}")
print("Unconstrained output tokens:", resp_a.metrics.accumulated_usage.get("outputTokens"))

# Constrained -- fresh agent so the second call's usage isn't cumulative with the first
agent2 = Agent(model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5"))
resp_b = agent2(
    f"Ticket: {ticket}\n\n"
    'Respond with only a JSON object: {"issue": string, "urgency": "low"|"medium"|"high"}. '
    "No other text."
)
print("Constrained output tokens:", resp_b.metrics.accumulated_usage.get("outputTokens"))
print("Constrained output:", str(resp_b))

exercises.costImpact: Output-token savings apply per call. At 10,000 calls/day, a drop from ~300 to ~40 output tokens is roughly 2.6M tokens/day saved, with no infrastructure change — just the instruction text.

exercises.title: Compress a narrative system prompt into a dense instruction set
exercises.goal: Rewrite a prose-style system prompt as structured bullets and measure the token delta using native Bedrock token counting, without losing any instruction.
steps: Take (or write) a system prompt in narrative style, e.g. 3-4 sentences of paragraph prose explaining the agent's role and constraints.

Build an agent with that system prompt and use_native_token_count=True, send one placeholder message, and read input tokens from accumulated_usage. → Expect: a baseline number that includes the system prompt.
Rewrite the same guidance as short imperative bullets, one instruction per line, removing connective prose. Build a second agent with the dense version and repeat.

Compare the two input token counts. → Expect: fewer tokens for materially the same instructions, since prose connectives ('In addition, you should also make sure to...') cost tokens without adding constraint.

code.content:
from strands import Agent
from strands.models import BedrockModel

narrative = (
    "You are a helpful assistant that works for our customer support team. "
    "It is very important that you always remain polite and professional at all times, "
    "and you should try your best to resolve the customer's issue. In addition, you should "
    "also make sure to never make promises about refund timelines, since only a human agent "
    "is authorized to do that, and you should always ask for the order number if the customer "
    "has not already provided one."
)

dense = (
    "Role: customer support assistant.\n"
    "- Be polite and professional.\n"
    "- Never promise refund timelines (human-only).\n"
    "- Always request the order number if missing."
)

for label, system_prompt in [("narrative", narrative), ("dense", dense)]:
    model = BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", use_native_token_count=True)
    agent = Agent(model=model, system_prompt=system_prompt)
    response = agent("Hello")
    print(label, response.metrics.accumulated_usage.get("inputTokens"))

exercises.costImpact: System prompt tokens are paid on every call. A saving of even 30-40 tokens per call compounds linearly with volume and, unlike output-format savings, applies even to calls that produce no useful output (retries, errors, tool-only turns).

sources.claim: General guidance on being explicit and specific in prompts, and on output formatting as a controllable variable.

sources.title: Anthropic — Reduce latency (applies to output-length control)
sources.claim: Output length is a primary driver of both latency and cost; constraining format is the direct lever.
